observation.visible_scene: A macro close-up of a bundle of colored pencils (or crayon-like sticks) against a pure black background. On the left and center the shafts hang vertically, their cut ends facing the camera at staggered heights and revealing colored cores (white, red, yellow, orange, green, pink, magenta, dark red, brown, purple, light blue, dark blue). On the right a separate horizontal row of cut ends (wooden rings with dark/colored cores) projects toward the viewer. Faint colored glows appear as reflections on the dark surface below in later frames.
visible_changes: The vertically hanging pencils translate up and down independently, each at its own phase/amplitude, so the line of their cut ends ripples rather than moving as a rigid block (e.g., the red-tipped shaft rises early then descends, while the white and yellow shafts drift downward over the clip).
The horizontal row of cut ends on the right also shifts slightly downward and its spacing relative to the vertical group changes modestly.
A soft reddish (and later bluish) reflection becomes visible on the bottom edge that is absent or very dim in the first frames.
The overall framing shows a slight scale/position drift, but the differing vertical offsets among individual pencils indicate real object motion, not a uniform camera pan.
outside_clip_unknowns: What drives the bobbing (a hand, a motor, vibration, or the pencils being shaken) is not shown.
Whether the oscillation is settling, continuing, or just captured mid-cycle at both crop boundaries is unknown.
The full length of the shafts above the top edge and any context beyond the bundle are unseen.
uncertain_details: The exact split between camera zoom/drift and pencil translation is hard to fix because the background is featureless.
Whether the horizontal row moves on its own or merely follows a slight camera shift is ambiguous.
The appearance of the bottom reflections could be a lighting change or a camera angle change rather than an object event.
